## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sabbamatthītikathā* ("Discussion of 'Everything Exists'") is the sixth debate of the first book or chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, located in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Watanabe 1983]. Within the dialectical structure of the *Kathāvatthu*, it represents a formal Sthaviravādin refutation of the core proposition maintained by the Sarvāstivāda school that past, present, and future dharmas exist (*sabbam atthi*), using systematic logical methods of interrogative refutation [Watanabe 1983; Kragh 2013]. Modern scholarship has analyzed the text as a central Theravādin critique of Sarvāstivādin ontological and temporal theories [Kragh 2013].
The controversy hinges extensively on canonical definitions of existence and time. SuttaCentral records intertextual ties between this debate and several Nikāya suttas, notably the *Niruttipathasutta* (SN 22.62), *Khandhasutta* (SN 22.48), *Atthirāgasutta* (SN 12.64), *Phaggunapañhāsutta* (SN 35.83), *Mahācattārīsaka Sutta* (MN 117), *Sāḷhasutta* (AN 3.66), and *Paribbājakasutta* (AN 4.30), as well as passages in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 14) and *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 2) [SuttaCentral]. Confirming these canonical foundations, DharmaNexus identifies thousands of shared textual matches across Pali literature, led by large shared segments with the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), and the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits high internal reuse with related *Kathāvatthu* chapters on temporality and ontology, including the *Atītakkhandhādikathā* (Kv 1.7), the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), the *Ekaccaṁatthītikathā* (Kv 1.8), and the commentary (*Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus computes cross-language alignments with Chinese Āgamas (*Saṁyuktāgama* T 99, *Madhyamāgama* T 26, and *Ekottarikāgama* T 125) and Mahāyāna philosophical treatises such as the *Tattvasaṃgrahapañcikā* and Prajñāpāramitā literature [DharmaNexus].
